# Choose a License

> Non-judgmental guidance for selecting appropriate open source licenses for software and hardware projects.

Choose a License provides comprehensive resources for understanding and comparing open source licenses, from permissive licenses like MIT to strong copyleft licenses like GNU GPLv3. The site serves as an authoritative reference for developers, projects, and communities navigating software licensing decisions.

## Key Topics

- Open Source Licenses
- MIT License
- GNU GPLv3
- GNU GPLv2
- Apache License 2.0
- Copyleft
- Permissive Licenses
- Patent Rights
- Source Code Disclosure
- License Selection
- Commercial Use
- Copyright Notice
- Free Software
- License Comparison
- Software Licensing

## Core Resources

- [Choose an open source license](https://choosealicense.com): Homepage: non-judgmental guidance for choosing open source licenses
- [What's this about?](https://choosealicense.com/about): About Choose a License: mission and open source licensing guidance

## License Comparison & Reference

- [Licenses](https://choosealicense.com/licenses): Comprehensive comparison of open source licenses and conditions
- [Appendix](https://choosealicense.com/appendix): Comprehensive reference table of open source licenses and details

## Popular Licenses

- [MIT License](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/mit): MIT License details: permissive, simple, allows commercial use
- [GNU General Public License v3.0](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/gpl-3.0): GNU GPLv3 details: strong copyleft, requires source disclosure
- [GNU General Public License v2.0](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/gpl-2.0): GNU GPLv2 details: widely-used strong copyleft free software license
- [Mozilla Public License 2.0](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/mpl-2.0): Mozilla Public License 2.0: weak copyleft with file-level requirements
- [Eclipse Public License 2.0](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/epl-2.0): Eclipse Public License 2.0: commercially-friendly copyleft license

## Specialized & International Licenses

- [European Union Public License 1.2](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/eupl-1.2): EUPL 1.2: EU-approved copyleft license in 23 official languages
- [Mulan Permissive Software License, Version 2](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/mulanpsl-2.0): Mulan PSL v2: OSI-approved permissive license in Chinese and English
- [Blue Oak Model License 1.0.0](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/blueoak-1.0.0): Blue Oak Model License: permissive with notice requirement and patent grant
- [LaTeX Project Public License v1.3c](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/lppl-1.3c): LaTeX Project Public License: primary license for LaTeX distribution
- [CERN Open Hardware Licence Version 2 - Weakly Reciprocal](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/cern-ohl-w-2.0): CERN-OHL-W: weakly reciprocal open hardware license from CERN
- [Microsoft Reciprocal License](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/ms-rl): Microsoft Reciprocal License: reciprocal with patent grant provisions
- [BSD 3-Clause Clear License](https://choosealicense.com/licenses/bsd-3-clause-clear): BSD 3-Clause Clear: permissive variant without patent rights grant

## Licensing Guidance

- [Existing projects and communities](https://choosealicense.com/community): Guide to license selection for existing open source projects and communities
- [Non-Software Licenses](https://choosealicense.com/non-software): Guide to Creative Commons and non-software licensing options
- [No License](https://choosealicense.com/no-permission): Guidance on opting out of open source licenses and copyright implications
